domains.name: Understanding the basics of dangerous goods
Indicators within documentation of undeclared dangerous goods

editorial.meta_description: The IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations certification validates your professional ability to manage, classify, and document hazardous materials for safe air.
editorial.overview: The IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR) certification, administered by IATA, validates your ability to manage hazardous shipments. This exam covers the classification, packing, labeling, and documentation of dangerous goods for air transport. It ensures that personnel understand the regulatory requirements necessary to maintain safety and efficiency when handling, storing, and reporting dangerous goods in accordance with international standards. By achieving this certification, professionals demonstrate their commitment to safety and compliance within the aviation industry, ensuring that all hazardous materials are processed correctly and safely according to the established global standards for air transport.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is intended for airline staff, freight forwarders, ground handlers, and shippers. Professionals responsible for the classification, packing, or documentation of hazardous materials in air transport should take this exam to ensure compliance with international regulations and safety standards.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the current IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations manual to understand the procedures. Focus on the classification of hazardous materials and the specific requirements for documentation and incident reporting. Practice identifying hidden dangerous goods within shipping documents. Ensure you are familiar with the 30 questions you will face during the 75-minute exam to manage your time effectively. Consistent study of the regulatory framework is required for success.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the fundamental concepts and regulatory framework governing the transport of dangerous goods by air, including the specific responsibilities of shippers and operators to ensure safety and compliance throughout the entire logistics chain.

This domain focuses on the identification and classification of hazardous materials, including explosives, gases, and toxic substances, to ensure safe handling and transport in accordance with the strict requirements set forth by international aviation authorities.
study_focus: Identification of toxic and corrosive materials

domain_guidance.summary: This domain addresses the identification of undeclared dangerous goods within shipping documentation and the verification of air waybills and shipper declarations to prevent the accidental transport of prohibited or improperly labeled hazardous materials by air.

This domain covers the procedures for reporting accidents and incidents involving dangerous goods, including document retention and information provision to ensure that all safety protocols are followed after any potential hazardous material event occurs.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: You will have 75 minutes to complete 30 questions. Ensure you meet the 80% correct answers requirement to pass. Review your documentation and classification knowledge before starting the exam to ensure accuracy and confidence during the assessment process.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR) certification exam consists of exactly 30 questions. You must be prepared to answer these within the allotted time to successfully complete the assessment and earn your professional certification.

To pass the IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR) certification, you must achieve a score of 80% correct answers. This threshold ensures that all certified professionals possess the necessary knowledge to handle hazardous materials safely.

The exam is a 75-minute assessment designed to test your knowledge of dangerous goods regulations. You should manage your time carefully throughout the session to ensure you have sufficient opportunity to address every question provided.

faq.question_title: Where can I find the current certification path?
faq.answer_text: This certification is current. For information regarding the long-term certification path or future requirements, check with IATA for the current certification path. They provide the most accurate and up-to-date guidance for maintaining your professional standing in the aviation industry.
